blocks.text: Transfer molding is a manufacturing process used to produce precision components from thermoset rubber, silicone, and engineered thermoset plastic materials.

During the process, a measured amount of uncured material is placed into a heated transfer chamber, commonly referred to as a pot. A plunger applies pressure, forcing the material through runners and gates into a closed mold cavity.
Heat and pressure cause the material to cure into its final shape. Once cured, the mold opens and the finished component is removed.
Unlike compression molding, where material is generally placed directly into an open mold cavity, transfer molding introduces material into an already closed mold.
This approach provides controlled material flow and can be especially useful when manufacturing parts with intricate features, embedded components, or bonded inserts.
Advantages of Transfer Molding

items.text: Supports detailed features and challenging component designs.
Allows metal inserts, pins, bushings, and other compatible components to be incorporated into the finished part.
Produces integrated elastomer and metal assemblies.
Controlled material flow supports repeatable production when properly engineered.
Accommodates a range of thermoset rubber, silicone, and rigid thermoset plastic formulations.
Suitable for a variety of production volumes depending on part design, tooling, and material requirements.

blocks.text: Transfer molding can provide an effective balance of part complexity, manufacturing precision, and tooling economics.
SYNC offers specialized transfer molding solutions for custom components requiring engineered materials, complex geometries, and dependable manufacturing processes.
Rubber Transfer Molding
Rubber transfer molding is used to produce custom elastomer components requiring precision features, dimensional control, and material performance.
Typical applications include seals, gaskets, grommets, protective components, bushings, and industrial rubber assemblies.
Rubber transfer molding can be particularly useful when parts contain molded-in metal components or geometries that are difficult to manufacture using conventional compression molding.
Silicone Transfer Molding
Silicone transfer molding supports flexible components requiring temperature resistance, sealing performance, and long-term material stability.
Applications may include specialized seals, protective components, electrical insulation, and components used in demanding industrial and medical equipment.
Material selection and manufacturing processes are evaluated based on the intended operating environment and customer specifications.
Thermoset Plastic Transfer Molding
SYNC also offers transfer molding solutions for rigid thermoset plastic components.
Unlike flexible elastomers, rigid thermoset plastics are selected for applications requiring properties such as dimensional stability, mechanical strength, heat resistance, or electrical insulation.
Transfer molding can be particularly effective when components contain intricate geometries, molded-in terminals, embedded inserts, or complex internal features.
Insert Molding & Encapsulation
Transfer molding can integrate metal inserts, electrical contacts, threaded components, and other compatible materials directly into a molded part.

sections.heading: Transfer Molding vs. Compression Molding vs. Injection Molding

blocks.text: Each molding process offers unique manufacturing advantages.
Compression Molding
Often effective for larger components, simpler geometries, and applications where direct material placement into the mold provides manufacturing benefits.
Transfer Molding
Often preferred for parts with complex features, embedded inserts, or bonding requirements that benefit from material flowing into a closed mold.
Injection Molding
Can offer production efficiency and repeatability for higher-volume applications, depending on material selection, component design, and tooling investment.
SYNC offers multiple molding processes, allowing our technical teams to evaluate the manufacturing approach best suited to each customer's requirements.

faq.q: What is transfer molding used for?

a.text: Transfer molding is commonly used for custom rubber, silicone, and thermoset plastic components with complex geometries, molded-in inserts, or specialized performance requirements.
Typical products include seals, grommets, bushings, electrical components, and bonded assemblies.

faq.q: What is the difference between transfer molding and compression molding?

a.text: Compression molding typically places material directly into an open mold before closing and curing it.
Transfer molding forces material from a separate chamber into an already closed mold, providing controlled flow into cavities and around embedded components.

faq.q: Can transfer molding be used for rubber-to-metal bonding?

a.text: Yes. Transfer molding can be particularly effective for components requiring molded rubber bonded to prepared metal inserts.

faq.q: Can thermoset plastics be transfer molded?

a.text: Yes. Transfer molding is used with rigid thermoset materials such as phenolic, epoxy, and other engineered thermoset compounds.

faq.q: Is transfer molding suitable for low-volume production?

a.text: Yes. Transfer molding can support low-, medium-, and high-volume production, depending on tooling requirements, component geometry, material selection, and manufacturing economics.

faq.q: What information is needed to request a quote?

a.text: Providing a part drawing or 3D model, material specifications, estimated annual volume, quality requirements, and application information helps our engineering team evaluate the project.
If you're unsure which molding process is appropriate, SYNC can help review the available options.
